description: F-CORE-039: a tenant says what it IS, and the pack turns that into a date. `appropriateResult` could book a resolution but not say whether one was owed or by when, and both answers depend on the legal form as much as on the jurisdiction — so the pack carries a catalogue and the core carries only the arithmetic: fiscal-year end plus n months, rounded up to the end of that month. The pack here is deliberately fictional, because what is under test is mechanism, not German law: a form that owes a resolution in eight months, eleven when the entity is small, and a form that owes none at all. `required: false` is an ANSWER — the projection reports `false` and no date, which an application must be able to tell apart from `null`, meaning nobody has said what this company is. Note the fiscal year: it ends 30 November, so the deadline is 31 July of the year after next and not 30 July — the statutes of this kind read "within the first n months of the following financial year", and plain month arithmetic is a day short. The two refusals come first and leave nothing behind: `auditLog` counts two records, one per resolution that was actually accepted.

steps.comment: A form the pack does not know is refused by name, with the offered list attached — a screen can build itself from the refusal.
And so is a size class it does not grade by. Silently ignoring it would report the regular deadline as if it were the graded one.
Small entities get longer. The size class is declared, not computed — nobody can derive a headcount from a journal.
